description: Replication of Gelman, Silver, Edlin (2012), 'What is the probability your vote will make a difference?', Economic Inquiry 50(2). Probability that one vote is decisive = P(state's electoral votes are needed) x P(state is tied | needed). Forecast = actual state results (we do not have Silver's 2008 forecast) plus correlated uncertainty.

uncertainty.calibration_note: Chosen on 2008 (1M sims each, sweep 0.02-0.07 national, 0.03-0.04 state): national 0.06 / state 0.03 gives average 1 in 71M (paper 60M), NH tie given needed 1 in 80k (paper 70k), Ohio 2.9e-8 (3.1e-8), DC 1.3e-12 (2e-12), California needed 22% (18%). Means are actual results, not Silver's forecast, so New Mexico (actual Obama +15) is lower than in the paper.

method: Gelman-Silver-Edlin method on our own simulations; forecast = actual results; t(4) national + state errors.
